diagnosis: Mid-cycle upgrade on the 14th triggers proration of the remaining days on the old plan combined with the new Business plan charge, so the first invoice can exceed the plan list price. Invoice INV-88213 should show a proration credit line plus the new plan charge. No escalation required; this is an expected billing pattern per kb-0001.
reply: Thanks for reaching out about invoice INV-88213. Because your account upgraded to Business partway through the billing cycle, the first invoice includes proration: a credit for the unused days on your previous plan followed by a charge for the new Business plan. This is why the total can differ from the plan's list price for the first invoice only. If you review the invoice, you should see these proration lines itemized. If the amounts still don't look right after checking, reply with the specific line you're disputing and the amount you expected, and we'll take a closer look.
